notes.title: Build your own spaceship body as you fly in Jitter, an asteroid-heavy physics-based survival sim
notes.content:
I guess the simplest way to describe Jitter is that it's Heat Signature, the hectic spaceship hijacking game from Suspicious Developments, but you are the spaceship, not the hijacker, and also, you can glue pieces of other ships onto yourself, like in Captain Forever, and also, this looks a bit like Lemmings on the Game Boy. Boil that down, and we have a brand new subgenre, the Hot Lemming Boy Foreverlike, which... let's maybe forget I wrote the words "Hot Lemming Boy Foreverlike". Let's proceed without further reflection to this video showcasing the combat.

Read more

notes.title: Demo Update: What's New?
notes.content: [p][b]Hello to all space enthusiasts![/b][/p][p]If you look at the night sky right now, you might see a lot of meteors—these are the [b]Perseids[/b], dust clusters our planet is moving through. I tried to see some yesterday and I think I saw one! While that’s more than nothing, it's not the main topic today.[/p][p]This is the [b]final demo update[/b] before we enter Early Access, and that’s because we've added all the main features we planned! We're still polishing the mechanics and balancing the game, but I hope with your help we can get it all done.[/p][p]So, let’s get to the list of new features.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/bb3764ee31080f5cc6a02fa680da65e073577499.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]Ship Weapons & PvE Combat[/h3][p][/p][p]You can now find a variety of weapons in the game:  [b]railgun[/b], [b]industrial laser[/b], [b]mortar[/b], [b]rocket launcher[/b], [b]EMI cannon[/b], [b]graviton[/b], and [b]plasma cannon[/b].[/p][p]To help you get familiar with the new combat mechanics, we've created a separate tutorial level. You won't miss it! You can also find different weapon types in the demo and sandbox levels. Cutting various objects with a laser is especially fun.[/p][p]You can also meet different enemies now:[/p][list][*][p][b]Drones[/b] are dangerous but vulnerable. The best way to deal with them is with a plasma grenade—it'll smash them to pieces.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Larger ships[/b] (similar to octopuses) have a powerful protective field in front, so approach them from the tail.[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]EMI cannon[/b] is also a great tool; it neutralizes enemies for a short time.[/p][/*][/list][p]Enemies will defend their zone or patrol a route, but if you get into their line of sight, they will attack. A good tactic is to knock the weapon modules off an enemy. They'll be left without a way to fight back and will start to run away. Give it a try![/p][p][/p][h3]Gamepad & SteamDeck Support[/h3][p][/p][p]Flying with a [b]gamepad[/b] is a special treat—be sure to try it and let us know what you think. We've added partial support so you can dock, select different devices, and control them. The gamepad also works with the user interface almost everywhere.[/p][p]We’ve also added new hints for those playing on a gamepad and updated the keyboard and mouse hints. We are still making some changes to our control solutions and would love to hear your feedback and advice.[/p][p][/p][h3]Other Improvements & Bug Fixes[/h3][p][/p][p]These are the big features, but we've also made many small changes and bug fixes. Of course, a number of new bugs have likely been introduced that we haven't caught yet.[/p][p]Among the smaller features:[/p][list][*][p]A new approach to the [b]field of view[/b] that uses ray tracing and changes shape, especially in caves.[/p][/*][*][p]The [b]control panel[/b] now generates and stores a small amount of energy, so you can fly to the nearest generator even if your batteries run out.[/p][/*][*][p]We've also had a few [b]optimization sessions[/b] that have paid off—everything is running faster. I recommend playing in full-screen mode for the best experience.[/p][/*][/list][p]And of course, we're preparing a large open world that will tell a story... I hope you'll find out what it is soon.[/p][p]Enjoy the update, and let us know what you think![/p]

notes.title: Dev Update #3
notes.content:
[p][b]Hello, Community![/b][/p][p]This post is a bit of an impromptu update, driven by a strong desire to share what we’re currently working on.[/p][p]Development is ongoing, and it’s worth noting — these are the final major updates before our Early Access release. So stay with us — it’s all coming together!
It's not easy working under drone and missile strikes, but your attention and support should remain focused on the game itself. The circumstances — that’s our personal matter.[/p][p]So, the first thing we want to show is [b]path planning[/b]. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/c13ecb3404c32b8201e4da18dba0da60872dac62.gif"][/img][/p][p]Now bots, drones, and other ships can move around obstacles and find paths. It wasn’t easy — we’ve posted about it on Twitter — but we made it work. Enemy ships will chase you, combat drones will guard areas, and shuttles will fly between asteroids, avoiding them in a dynamically changing physical environment.[/p][p]And of course — [b]ship weapons[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/1f6fb61e5c8b6c41598a40270fd1845422b7c3df.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/ab98884685ffdee29f66b14bba9169d7ac68e678.gif"][/img]
Missiles, plasma cannons, railguns, gravity guns, EMPs, and mortars — this is just the beginning. The system allows us to quickly add new types of weapons with different parameters. We also plan to include unique and rare weapons.[/p][p]Soon, we’ll be arming other ships and starting to balance space combat between players and bots.[/p][p]Another big challenge for us is [b]adapting the game for controllers and Steam Deck[/b].
Flying with a controller is awesome, but managing your ship with one — that’s another challenge. Still, we’re making good progress and we’ll show it soon.[/p][p]We’ll update the demo with new combat levels and will try to add controller support as well.[/p][p]I’ve spilled all our plans and secrets — but I don’t mind. Everything is coming together beautifully, and we’ll all benefit from it.[/p][p]To follow development more closely — subscribe to our [url="https://x.com/JitterGame"]Twitter[/url] or [url="https://discord.gg/mucJ4UQ"]Discord[/url]. That’s where we post the latest news and in-progress feature videos.[/p][p][b]Wishing you a great day and a peaceful night![/b][/p]

notes.title: Demo update!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/60061d90e954944679c999fc34bcc8bca35f8ba4.png[/img]
[h2]Key bindings[/h2]
First and foremost, check out the control settings. You can customize your key bindings, and we’re eager to hear your feedback. It’s important for us to know what feels most comfortable for you, as it will help us define the best default configuration.

[h2]Gamepad support[/h2]
You can also fly using a gamepad. Currently, not all mechanics are fully compatible, but flying, docking, and undocking work smoothly. By default, the gamepad is used in dialogues, although not consistently across all menus. You may still need to use the mouse occasionally.

[h2]Seamless world support[/h2]
We’ve worked on creating seamless transitions between different sectors, allowing for potentially endless worlds without loading screens. There’s still some fine-tuning to do, but overall, it’s functioning well. We’ve also redesigned the Playground, transforming it into an open world with seamless transitions.

[h2]Minimap[/h2]
To help you navigate the levels more easily, we’ve added a mini-map. You can open it to view the entire level. Additionally, you can place your own marker on the mini-map by right-clicking.

[h2]Recycler[/h2]
We’ve introduced a new tutorial level featuring a recycler and revamped the air level. It looks quite engaging, so don’t miss out on trying it. You’ll also find recyclers on other levels.

[h2]Support for large screens[/h2]
We’ve added game scaling for large screen resolutions, ensuring that 4K monitor owners won’t struggle with tiny text. We’re keen to get feedback from our 4K users!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/afd96ecbb634ab6d52b2086edecb753d9b1653d1.png[/img]

There are still some bugs, but we’re actively working on fixing them. With your help, we aim to polish the game and make a great impression at Next Fest!

notes.title: Jitter was the best in two categories at the Games Gathering!
notes.content:
Recently we have been working on several features and also added a minimap. We wanted to take part in the conference to test the work of new mechanics on players. This year there were many interesting projects and you can learn about them on our [url=https://x.com/JitterGame/status/1866133973849555389]twitter[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/0f58946b394fd21b8e727d60cb2a6ca01052f215.png[/img]
We received a lot of useful feedback and comments and were pleasantly surprised by winning in two nominations: the best game presented at the conference and also the best gameplay!

This really lifted our spirits and now we have a charge to work. In the near future we will do the work on the bugs and publish an update for the demo with new features.

Also now we will definitely have an open world. Big as space.

notes.title: Some development news #2
notes.content:
[h2]Hello everyone![/h2]

We’re thrilled by the interest in our game and grateful for the amazing community that's growing around it. Your feedback and suggestions have been invaluable—thanks to everyone sharing ideas on Discord! We've built up quite a list, and we're excited to bring as many of your suggestions to life as possible.

We know the demo still has its share of bugs and rough spots, but we’re steadily working on improvements. Here’s a quick look at what’s in development:

[b]Key Binding and Gamepad Support[/b]

We're focusing on key binding and gamepad compatibility, which means Steam Deck support is also in the works! This won’t happen overnight, but we’re making progress, and these features will definitely be included in early access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/52386d11cf037d676c1c8c3a727a377b7c5d8e1c.gif[/img]
[b]Recycler Mechanic[/b]

Another big feature under development is the recycler, a tool with a wide range of uses. It’s a complex addition, but we’re committed to making it versatile and useful. With its complexity, we expect more bugs to pop up, but we’re dedicating resources to fix and optimize as much as we can.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/8092be024ce3fa3cb9042d8d45feaea4e496e336.gif[/img]

[b]Expanding the Story and World[/b]

We're actively building our story and the world. One upcoming mission, for instance, will challenge players to move massive tructures, adding an exciting layer to gameplay.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/150bd861dbd92a9a4993e855b8a3814b1de0f5a9.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/150bd861dbd92a9a4993e855b8a3814b1de0f5a9.gif[/img][/url]

We’re aiming to release an updated demo by the beginning of winter. Thank you all for the incredible support—it means so much to us to feel connected to each of you who’s cheering us on.

See you soon!

notes.title: Jitter Demo is Released!
notes.content:
The demo contains a full titorial and introduces players to life aboard the Ankora mining station in the Main Asteroid Belt, presenting a self-contained story from the Jitter universe.

The second level is a sandbox environment that allows players to experiment with Jitter’s diverse gameplay systems, including spacecraft navigation, physics-based puzzles, air and energy subsystems management, module docking and repairs, as well as a strategic crew command layer.

Please, feel free to share your thoughts on demo on Steam forums or our Discord.

notes.title: Some development news
notes.content:
[b]Hello everybody! [/b]

I would like to address the followers and tell about our news. But first I want to thank you for your support! We will definitely not disappoint you - there is a lot of interesting stuff ahead. As a team, we really want to release a great game and exactly the way we intended it to be.

And now [b]some[/b] development [b]news[/b].

We are currently preparing a demo version for publication here on Steam. It should be a good demo version and most importantly - understandable from the player's point of view. The game has a lot of mechanics and we are currently making a tutorial with hints.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44983133/75253928f49100700123872a3fb276981519bc30.gif[/img]

Also added such mechanics as power shields, fire and its interaction with air.
We are also making many improvements to the interface. After the play tests, we have comments from the players and gradually implement their wishes.

Thanks again for your support and see you soon!

notes.title: FTL slams into Noita in this new sci-fi spaceship exploration sim
notes.content:
Not all AIs are evil, at least, ones in fiction aren't. In Jitter, an upcoming indie sci-fi exploration game, you play as an AI plugged into a spaceship. Tasked with taking care of your crew and your ship, it's safe to say that you're probably not evil. Well, maybe a little evil; we simply don't know yet. What we do know is that Jitter has just been unveiled and it's looking like a tasty mashup of FTL and Noita.
